answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by verifying identities through radar echo mapping of unique topography. Nodes prove physical presence by pinging an assigned knoll with high-frequency RF pulses to measure site-specific multipath delay spreads. An attacker incurs heavy capital costs procuring and positioning dedicated physical transceivers rather than spinning up virtual instances. However, dynamic clutter like a passing sparrow can alter the return pulse, causing false-positive rejections.
